steps.name: Victorian Soldier A
steps.text: Erk...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier B
steps.text: Ghakh!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier C
steps.text: Watch out—!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Next.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier D
steps.text: Heyaaaargh!!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Reporting in, sir!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: With Colonel Harold's support, we've brought all our current casualties back to safety!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: However, as things stand for us, we still don't have a way to strike the enemy where it hurts!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Charge!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Make use of your arms! The enemy is one soldier! Surround her!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Sir, wouldn't it be better for us to divert around her?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: She's an army of one! She's got not hope of holding us if we just widen the front!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: You... gormless idiot!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Was that meant to be a revelation to me?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Then why...

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: They didn't give you eyes in your head for nothing!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: You saw what our men on Kjeragandr's doorstep were attempting, didn't you? All of them as smart as you, off to break the perimeter from somewhere else!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Compare that to the rest! Are they in as near as bad a state?

spans.text: Compare that to the rest! Are
in as near as bad a state?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Sir, you're not telling me...

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Private, I don't know what the hell I could be telling you—DUCK!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Guh...!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: My hand slipped.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Done gossiping?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: When in the hell did you get here...?!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Just now.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you were counting on a few dozen men there to stop me, then you really weren't ready for me.

spans.text: If you were counting on a few dozen men there to stop me, then you

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Tsk! Monster incarnate...

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: A few dozen won't do the trick? Then surely a few hundred will. How about over a thousand?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: You'll learn. In the face of a real army, there is no army of one—

spans.text: You'll learn. In the face of a real army, there

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Clench your teeth.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Keep your mouth shut when I hit you.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You don't want to bite your tongue.
A bitter slice of wind whistles through.
One against two thousand should be the pinnacle of despair. Her golden eyes tell of no such qualms—stern and still and steady.
She is the predator without dispute. She is the ruler over this battlefield.
Slight the affairs of one Ms. Degenbrecher, dare to even begin to scorn her, and you too are an affront to her.
—You'd best hope your own life meant as little to you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Steady now, Madam Degenbrecher!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If my subordinates have cocked up talks with you, then it falls to me to apologize in their stead.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And how long can you shield them for?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well! Ha-hah. Might I suggest... until I die a soldier's death?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *hiss*...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm no match for your namesakes! Clearly I've not the horns to lock with you in a fight.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Do you recall, Madam Degenbrecher, when I asked after your name?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I no longer see any time like the present. Might I be elucidated?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You have the guts to stall with me?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *wheeze*, *wheeze*!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Two of a mind can spare a word in no-man's land! It is done, you know... it's the done thing!

spans.text: Two of a mind can spare a word in no-man's land! It
done, you know... it's the done thing!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I barely even remember my real name. You can pretend I never had one.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Plenty of people in Leithanien's ruined streets without a name or a home.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: —I'd heard tell of your Leithanian birth, but never had I known that to be your life's story...

spans.text: —I'd heard tell of your Leithanian birth, but
had I known that to be your life's story...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I once read in the dailies how you pilgrimed home there. Adulation of the masses. Dinners with the upper crust.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Throw a trophy at a burdenbeast and watch them love it too. They don't tell the difference.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Don't let it fool you.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's not a place where names change anything. No one's going to ask you when you're down in the gutter with the wastewater.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Yet now you've a name with... such power.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Power?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Not exactly.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It was a sunny day.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: A Gendarmerie patrol rounded up anyone with no place to go on the corner. One of them was carrying a strange weapon I'd never seen before. No point. No edge.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: No fine combat technique. No deep method to it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: No simpler way to bludgeon. No part was anything of mention. I watched as he took that thing to anybody who tried to resist, and caved in their skulls.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: From that moment on, it's been clear to me what I have.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Not a code, or a creed, or a technique. Nothing that sounds nice out loud.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's violence.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: So that day, I named myself.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I am what I wield.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: There's a Minoan school of thought, where they hold violence and victory as sisters. The two are inseparably close—they make one another.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A look at you, and I could be convinced.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher, if you're violence in the flesh like you say... then who, exactly, is your victory dedicated to?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And finally, one last little quibble from me—though I do think—it may not be worth much in the asking.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: That Gendarmerie who first enlightened you—was victory a sister to him too?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I did like his degenbrechers.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Good to use, but broke too fast.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Just like you, Craigavon.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Your arm's almost gone.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hush-hush, Madam Degenbrecher! Spare me the truth.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I do happen to be command of my own regiment. A little dignity, if you please...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Were the clock turned back thirty... no, just twenty years, I'd only be too glad your opponent.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But as it stands, and though I hate to admit it, the reality's all too obvious—I'm one of the old ones now.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You don't look it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah-ha, you think so too?!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Then I take it back—see, I've been telling them all, my mind's as sharp as ever!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's just this blasted prosthetic leg—the socket always stings on rainy days...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Less talk.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: How long until you give?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: How long until I give is hardly important.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What matters is, Madam Degenbrecher, how long until you give?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You can try me and see.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Now both sides have made their move.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: It seems Degenbrecher can still bear out for the moment. Harold is saving his strength, and his bombers and Casters are all but smelling the roses.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Your wine may not have been wasted after all, Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What of Weiss and Matterhorn?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I've sent a team of Tschäggättä to find them.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Given what reports have returned so far, the two were likely taken by surprise.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Viscount Craigavon wouldn't place them in mortal danger. That takes senility, and he has none.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: We can only hope.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Our people are en route to the station to stand by. They'll send us word immediately once they intercept.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: May it be that our guest arrives on time.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: What of the merchants that just contacted you?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: They won't be too daring for now.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis, pass word onto the Saintess for me—

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You can save that step!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I'm right here. If you have something to say, say it to me in person, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Saintess.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The Silverashes are disgraced to have allowed such a spiral of events on ceremony grounds. Once the ceremony is over, I will personally take myself to the Vine-Bead Court to apologize to you, Saintess.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But for now, I fear the ceremony will need to be postponed for another while.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: As it should. Your message is loud and clear, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If there is anything I can do, I ask you continue to come to me directly.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And not exploit that my own conscience might force me to see you first.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Saintess, praise thy benevolence.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But you and the Court devotees must be prudent right now. After you resume this ceremony yourself, Saintess, that will suffice to appease the people.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Degenbrecher's strength needs no introduction. A promise from her is exceedingly rare, and in the event she makes one, it's never broken.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I think we should give her our full confidence.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Is your confidence that Degenbrecher can fight one against a thousand, or that she has the disregard to die valiantly, in perfect service to your schemes?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Degenbrecher is ahead confronting the Victorians, and I know her mentality. She holds that, her own reputation aside, the slate with Kjerag can still be wiped clean should anything go wrong.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She... wait, did she tell you this herself?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: She defends Kjerag's dignity as one of Her plain, ordinary citizens.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Saintess, do you believe that I bluntly ordered her? Provoked her?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Even I might say she's changed some. Thus I've trusted her this once—I've gambled on her.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Had I not, you might have watched that affable Viscount lose his life to a few 'panicked tourists'.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We gamble for a best case scenario.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: 'Gamble'.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I have always considered the success or failure of anything to hinge on one's own grasp, and not entreaties to gods.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Nothing goes unaccounted for. I put all the chips down. I see it through, win or lose. I've never complained about it.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Unclasp your hands. You've bruised yourself.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I ask you pray for Degenbrecher, Great Saintess.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Weiss!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Wake up, Weiss!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Nngh...

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Matterhorn...?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Where... I...?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: —! Shit! The Victorians are changing it up! Their goal can't be that simple!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: We have to contact the Master!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Gk—*hiss*—

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Stay still, Weiss!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: If they even managed to subdue and lock up both you and me, then our squad's people can't have escaped either. I've tried, but brute strength alone isn't going to free us.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: It's light outside... It looks like it's day already.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Where are the Victorians?

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: All gone.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Unfortunately... they've probably swarmed the ceremonial grounds.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Matterhorn, help me out here.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: What do you need?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: I hide a razor in my shoe's upper.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: If you can just take it out, Matterhorn... and toss me it!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Don't be insane!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: What are you using that razor for? In your position? Do you not value your hands?!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: I have to try.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: The Master gave me this mission, and I couldn't complete it.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: And if that's forced him into a passive situation, then I...

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: In any case, even if I'm too late, and he doesn't need it, I'm still going to redeem what isn't lost! I have to make up for my disappointment!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: I suppose you're right.
Matterhorn heaves his body around, laying his fingers over the curve of Weiss's boot.

But what follows betrays Weiss's hopes. He doesn't toss the razor over, but instead pinches the paper-thin tool of murder between his fingers, and with great effort, strains and slashes at the rope over Weiss's wrists.
In its tenuous grip, the blade slips down between his fingers, and cuts into their pulp. Vivid red blood trickles down his wrist.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Matterhorn!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Your hand!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: It'll be fine. It's just a scratch.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: You were going to do the same thing, weren't you?

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: You do have a point, Weiss. The Master's expecting us. We can't leave him waiting too long.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Just give me one moment, and I can get this rope cut!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Matterhorn...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I'm not your enemy.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Sorry, you two were having a moment, weren't you?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Monch?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Didn't you leave Kjerag?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: About that... well, I'll explain in full later.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Madam Sciurus sent me out to scout. That's how I found you all tied up in this Victorian camp.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Where are the others?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I already set them free.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Anyway, both of you, get going. The Victorians kicked off battle at Lake Silberneherze.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: We need to be there as soon as we can.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Damn it! She can't hold for long!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: As if I can sit here and look on!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You get back here, Arctosz!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Do you seriously think you have the monopoly on righteous anger, Arctosz? We wish we could step in! If your eyes are shot, then try using your brain!

spans.text: Do you seriously think you have the monopoly on righteous anger, Arctosz? We
we could step in! If your eyes are shot, then try using your brain!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You acting will definitively ruin things!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Stooping behind others so I can feel sorry for myself runs counter to the Paleroche clan's blood!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I can't bear to see this!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Bear to see it, you baby!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Someone here is having a harder time watching than you, I guarantee.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Ten years that Degenbrecher's lived in Kjerag, hasn't she? Just to be some sacrificial pawn here?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: If today Enciodes can't settle all this, then no amount of achievement, no spoil for Kjerag, could ever convince me to lend him an ear again.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I'm far from the grand actor the rest of you would be! I cannot be as calm as any of you are!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: And it's too little, too late for that.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: All you and I can do now is believe in her.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I won't be arranging treatment for your wounded hands, then. Remember to hide it with gloves when the time comes.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Also, I imagine the Tschäggättä's report aligns with your gut.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: We can't count on Degenbrecher lasting much longer.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: She's no longer evading.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: She's acting how she used to in her Kazimierz competition days.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Only, afterwards...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Afterwards, as she fled the assassins with you, she amended that habit.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Any lack of care by her at that point, and you'd die sooner than she did.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Quite.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Still no word from your end?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: None.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: My investigators already returned. They're sure your guest boarded the train in question to Lake Silberneherze. If anything, it should have arrived just as the ceremony wound down.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: As it is, it'll still take some time until that train arrives.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis, never have I feared any wager.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Every step that I take, that I've ever taken, I've staked it all.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This time is no different.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I believe myself to be sufficiently prepared.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And yet, I find my patience is made of poorer stuff.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Thank you for telling me what's on your mind, and I know what you want to hear me say. I'll say it for you.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: If you want to ensure The Black Knight's life, or you don't believe she can last until the end, then give the order now. I can tell you, there are still odds of success.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: The archers and Casters at our call are best of the best. Blow up the lake's surface, create confusion, and draw the civilians and soldiers both into midwinter's icy pocket.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Enciodes, the decision lies with you—

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Whatever you do, I will support it. But whatever you do, you carry the consequences in kind.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Those consequences are no simple political game. You might fail to even bear them. That, I can determine for you.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: One quick question. If it were you?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Then the great winter swim would already be in full swing.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Let's trust in Degenbrecher.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Trust she won't fall.

a.text: At some unknown point, the first wound appears on her body.
It lies about her shoulder, a slash over her suit, an imperceptible trace of blood drawn.
Compared to the kinds of wounds she's used to, this one's worth no mention.
Degenbrecher fells the few soldiers about her. Ironically, the subtle sting only sharpens the heady mix of fear her eyes strike into you, makes her movements that much more steely cold.
The second wound is brought on by Originium Arts.
An average caster means nothing to Degenbrecher, but the numbers advantage mutates the nature of the Originium Arts' efficacy.
The casters among the troops cast behind their human wall. Fire, ice and thunder burst forth in unison, with staggering momentum.

Degenbrecher flings her weapons, running one of the casters' shoulders clean through, while she stubbornly approaches through the full length of their Arts' range, and plows straight into the soldiers' midst. That puts an end to that display.
The third wound comes as the artillerymen aim a third ballista volley at her.
An opponent armed to the teeth is no fear of Degenbrecher's, but with limbs less than free, and ballistae pestering her in spades, it does get a little annoying to cope.
A shell slips through, and lands a scorch mark on her abdomen.
Her skin is seared in an instant, but hardly any blood comes. That's good, all things considered.
Degenbrecher is under no impression she'll lose.
She's just not too sure she has enough blood to last much longer.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's not enough...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Again!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Urgh!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Lisburn!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Charles! Withdraw Lisburn to the rear!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You staunch his bleeding, I'll be right there with first aid—!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: *cough*...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier E
steps.text: She's giving out!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier F
steps.text: Now's our chance! Charge!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: As long as I can still move a finger...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Khakkhhh!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I can handle any of you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Surely you're reaching your limits too?!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If you really meant to fight us out-and-out, you wouldn't have drawn out this situation in the first place!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Fight like this any longer, and I fear death will come for somebody...

spans.text: Fight like this any longer, and I fear death

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Isn't that exactly the kind of war you Victorians make an art of starting?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The only difference here is, your opponent is me alone.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Harold, you're a soldier.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And I—am your enemy.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...Ha-hah, and keenly put, Madam Degenbrecher.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But I don't believe for a second that you're blind to it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Karlan Trade's private operations were ferreted out by the Trilby Ashers, and I don't think the Duke will rest on her laurels about it!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: That—*cough*—is Enciodes's problem.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This is the very last chance they're leaving Master Enciodes!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: He need only bend an ear to the Duke, he need only part with a sliver of the cake...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Be it just 30% of what we proposed! I could still take that back to the Duke and try, for heaven's sakes!

spans.text: Be it just 30% of what we proposed! I could still take that back to the Duke and

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This was never even a war you needed to win...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: How stupid.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Who do you say that as?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're window dressing. You're a tourist. You're a burdenbeast vet.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Have you been at leisure for so long, you've begun to believe your own lies?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: —No.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You've never forgotten who you are.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You hate war, absolutely.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You abandoned what real power was in your hands. You took what men of yours sympathized. You left the maelstrom far behind, and fled to Kjerag.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: To a land where you thought war could never really happen.

spans.text: To a land where you thought war could never

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: But you were still a Victorian inside.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It wasn't even something you had to remind yourself.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You might say that.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I am a Victorian soldier, Madam.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: That much is ordained, and I might loathe it, and I might flee it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But I could never sully Victoria's interests.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'm the same.
Is she the same as this Victorian?
They don't seem very identical.
She's Leithanien-born, Kazimierz-raised, and only then came to Kjerag.
They don't need to know her name. All they know is she's born to fight solo, a victor of the knight competitions, the only one to ever win three years running.
Turn the clock further back, and she's a freak cut off from Originium Arts, a pariah in Leithanien.
Gaining and losing any of these things is dead simple.
They bore her to death.
But now, what she has isn't so easily lost, and she has no plans to lose them.
Now, they are the same.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This dull chat—*cough*—ends here.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I feel all too sorry for you, Madam Degenbrecher.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, would that we hadn't come to this point. But if you wish it, then I choose to respect it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I must stress at this closing hour that I am, through and through, your fan. The show you made in besting each opponent dazzled like nothing else.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This and this alone I ask you to believe. It cannot be lied.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Noted.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's my honor.
Riddled with scars, she raises her degenbrechers once more.
Just as she did in her first appearance before them all, Degenbrecher's point stabs into the ice.
The mist, constant over Lake Silberneherze, parts. A subdued, gargantuan rumble sinks in her enemies' stomachs.
Kchk. Kchk.
There comes the fine sound of cracking, and it's deafening.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Time to end this.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: —! Order to all units!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Stop her breaking the ice! Regroup ASAP! Put down 'The Black Knight of Kazimierz'!
Nothing.
It's not in here.
Oh, and it's not here either.
Well, that just leaves...

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Excuse me, sir, the train is speeding up! If you must wander, then please watch your step!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Oh, right, you haven't received your complimentary gift yet, have you? Can I ask what you'd like?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: As compensation for your journey's delay, your purchase is completely free this time!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: But, sir, it's a free gift...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Then I give this gift to you, madam.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Er, but, that's not...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Now excuse me, if I could pass through?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: A—Alright!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: *huff*... *pant*...

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Urp... oh, what in the land?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: My legs are a little wobbly...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (Now, only the last cabin remains.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (After all this time running around, I'm ragged.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (I could retire... *sigh* Not when Londinium's still refinding its footing. Her Grace would never let me.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (What will I find behind this door?)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (Their Kjerag Defense, hidden until this very moment, buried deeper than even their covert transport routes...)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (Whatever it is, it's a shame.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: It's a shame—Silverash will never get to meet his...

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: What's up, panisko?

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: Sorry, we've got no seats left in our cabin. I think you want to try someplace else.

steps.name: Man In a Suit
steps.text: Uh, actually, I can just lea...

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: Did you need something, panisko?

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: I'm not kidding, we're full in here. I mean, you can see. We're bumping shoulders just trying to look around.

steps.name: Man in a Suit
steps.text: Yeah, that's why I'm saying I can absolutely just leave and find my own seat! I'm not kidding either!

steps.name: Man in a Suit
steps.text: You—You guys seriously don't gotta sit in a cab with me!

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: Don't be like that, Mr. Spokesman. You and us, we're invited together, aren't we? It was all one letter.

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: And this cabin, perfect amount of room for us all to sit. They look after you on the way too.

steps.name: Silver-clad Knight
steps.text: And with us around, the safety problem is no problem.

steps.name: Man in a Suit
steps.text: Safety's not my problem here, yeah, no...

steps.name: Man in a Suit
steps.text: I don't think it's 'perfect', is the thing?? You guys get to sit on the benches and I have to dump my butt on the table!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...Apologies, excuse me.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I see... I understand. I must be dreaming.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Kazimierz campaign knights and a KGCC representative spokesman sat in the same private cabin of a railway car...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: So this is the defense Silverash plays.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: How bold. How well and truly typical of the clan head's style.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Your Grace, I can't say it was for lack of trying...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But while duty might call me to fight a gaggle of campaign knights at once, I... think it's a little out of the question.
More than a little.
I guess your job's not easy either.

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: Stay calm.

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: Just passing through.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: That uniform...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...This is quite the surprise party.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: What is a Rhodes Islander doing here?

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: You'll have to ask my boss.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Quite the shocker indeed. I wasn't expecting you in the flesh.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But the funny thing is, weren't Rhodes Island and Kjerag only meant to be 'business partners'?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Yes, if there's one thing I can trust, it's my memory.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Many happy returns... 'Doctor'.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And we have a Rhodes Island Operator here? It seems the dossiers were right—we still haven't full stock of your company's many faces.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Still, that aside for now. No surprise could be more pleasant, meeting you here.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: In all sincerity, I come with open arms this time. After all, I'm not even out of this disguise, and you recognize me by it.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Rhodes Island, you—
Yeesh, Doctor! A little help here!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hmm? 'Sup?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Our stop's coming up! We gotta get the tech packed, Doc...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oop? Who're you guys...?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Doctor, maybe we oughta bug the conductor to go a little faster...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, it's you!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Rhodes Island and Columbia's Rhine Lab... well, well, well.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I see it's no coincidence you're all here, then.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh, jeez, I guess someone knows me already.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Doc, Mr. Sharp, Letobomb, aren't you gonna introduce this hatsy guy to me here?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr, I'd like to know. Would Kjeragandr bless the woman waging such a bloody battle for this statue?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Though she is born from other lands? Though in Kjeragandr, she has oh so little faith?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Heheh. That's a very easy question, Saintess.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: The term 'Kjerag' simply means one who lives there, who adores this land, who finds a home in this nation.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: It's no matter whether Kjeragandr recognizes it.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If a person identifies with it from the bottom of their heart, well, who can deny that?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: No one can deny that. Not even she, herself.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She is a Kjerag. She already was.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr, come with me to meet our visitors.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Our Victorian guests have come to partake in the ceremony. As Saintess, I have to make an adequate response.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: At the very least, I can't go without saying hello.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I'd like to stress—the danger of this.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: But... very well, Saintess.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Matriarch!

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Sciurus is back!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: She is?!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Some nerve being late... wait, no, I told her to keep out of this! Why did she come HERE?!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Who's saying I can't come?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: And I didn't just come, I brought some special guests with me too!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Is this let's-bring-guests timing to you?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You make a language out of inane, you silly sister!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: ...I am NOT being silly.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Indeed. Madam Sciurus's hand is deft and wise. I find her admirable.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Ratatos, you'd do well to finally raise your opinion of her.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: ...What the hell is this, Enciodes?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Madam Sciurus, the guests have arrived safely.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Good! Bring them all in!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I'm out.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Master!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Your guests are here already!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Your who? These are MY guests I invited!

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: You're Madam Sciurus of the Browntail clan?

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Very pleased you invited us to be part of this ceremony.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Sciurus... is this your pleasant surprise?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Uh, duh!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Let me introduce you all! We have here our campaign knight from the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz, here to celebrate the erection of our statue to Kjeragandr!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I sent an invitation especially to the Adeptus! That was NOT an easy invitation to make!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: So they're MY guests!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It's just a coincidence, Madam Sciurus.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I cannot laud you enough that you were able to invite a campaign knight. My guest of honor, meanwhile, would be this fellow—

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Welcome, Sir Spokesman of the General Chamber of Commerce.

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: Hello to you. I'm taking it you're Mr. Silverash?

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: Good to meetcha, good to meetcha, and hello from my company. Thank you for all the effort of inviting me out to Kjerag.

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: The scenery here in Kjerag, supremely beautiful. I believe your company and mine will absolutely end the day here with a partnership we both love.

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: Oh, and don't mind me but I gotta say, I think I saw some mad fight out on a frozen lake the whole way here?

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: And kind of familiar too, like, one guy. I mean, those combat moves, they rang bells in my head.

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: Oh sorry, excuse me if I'm talking too much?

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: It's, uh, a holdover from the old job. Ahem. Right, I'll be careful not to say too much that doesn't work towards us working together.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: No, Mr. Mob, I'm in need of your exact talent right now.

steps.name: Spokesman Mob
steps.text: Come again? You need...?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Right now, this very moment.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Please, come with me. I'll have them cast sound amplification Arts.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: May I ask you to loudly proclaim that—

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Karlan Trade, and the corporations of the Kazimierz General Chamber of Commerce, are about to sign an agreement.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: To Kazimierz, Kjerag will become a trusty partner.
...What's that noise?
It's not anyone splashing into the icewater, and it's not cries for help.
It sounds like someone loudly saying something, and then the people all about her stumble in disarray.
That loud voice. But whatever it's saying, she can't tell clearly.
Her field of view narrows and dims by a fraction more. The sounds almost turn to fuzz in her ears.
She can't feel her own limbs anymore, but she can be sure she still has a grip on her old companions.
Her degenbrechers.
Because she knows her body is still acting on reflex, striking down every person that comes near.
It's just... too loud.
Too loud. How can someone talk this noisily?
Why has the crowd gone?
Did someone breach her line of defense already?
No.
The wild beast's dulling eyes of gold suddenly flare alight.
—As long as she can stand.
—She will allow absolutely no one past!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...brecher! Madam Degenbrecher!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Stop fighting... Gah!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You've lost too much blood, Madam Degenbrecher! Come to your senses a little!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Aht-aht-aht, keep flailing at this rate and you'll sink us both in the lake!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: We're not fighting?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No more fighting, no more!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Goodness, however much the Duke wants to slap Kjerag in the face, we can't be showing Kazimierz the hand in the process... at least not now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Kept between Victoria and Kjerag, one might still call it the Duke's personal Silverash grievances. But the moment you bring Kazimierz into it too, things become far, far less simple.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Are the gourmands of Kazimierz already inviting Karlan Trade to the table? With such distance between them, and in such short order?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What a talented young individual.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And I know the Duke won't reproach me for deciding to stay my hand. Spiffing excuse.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A good half my men you batted into the lake, Madam Degenbrecher. It was a backbreaker to scoop them out again...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If we'd kept going like that, I'd need another pair of arms to treat you all!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: I say you need them as is. *cough*

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I take no criticism from anyone still hacking up blood.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: ...We're done?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well and truly done.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Okay.
Enciodes pulled it off.
She did what she needed to.
That's all Degenbrecher hears.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now, Madam, stop there!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The lives we live, they always tend to be out of our hands.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I wanted to retire eons ago myself, but I have to keep my own men, my all too often down-and-out brothers in mind.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: With this, it finally ought to be my turn for once, hm?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And in light of the fact your faithful fan's been beaten black and blue...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Could you give me your autograph?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: ...You're still in the mood for that?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This card... heh.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Do tell?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The first time I won the Major, they wouldn't leave me alone until I agreed to a photoshoot.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: After that, I never agreed to another one. They were too boring for me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I see. No wonder The Black Knight's knight trumps always come in those same poses, edition after edition.
Degenbrecher accepts the pen Harold holds out to her, and writes her name—'Degenbrecher'.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You'd better not have anything else for me to sign.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, Madam, where are you going?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Do you need some quick treatment? My first aid's excellent, you know.
Degenbrecher lifts her head to look to the dawn.
In the distance, two figures walk, approaching her. She still can't make them out, but she knows who they are.
It's like Kjeragandr on high is gazing down on her, someplace as high as the sun.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'm going back.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's people waiting for me.
